entries.title: Agent Skills — specification and documentation
entries.creator: Agent Skills project
entries.attribution: Agent Skills project. Apache-2.0 / CC-BY-4.0.
entries.observations: Skill as a directory (SKILL.md + scripts/references/assets), minimal required frontmatter, progressive disclosure so the agent loads the body only on demand. Adopted structurally for skills/; we add invariants, acceptance, and authority fields the spec does not require.
entries.notes: License is compatible, but nothing is copied — we implement the shape ourselves.

entries.title: AI detection tools adoption in academic publishing — 2026 trends
entries.creator: CASRAI
entries.observations: Publishing moved from AI-origin detection to editorial quality assessment. The checkable failure signatures — fabricated references, phantom citations, overstated claims, weak figure provenance, missing disclosure — map onto mechanisms already enforced in P0. Gap identified: we verify that a citation resolves, not that it supports the claim; that belongs in the eval fixtures.
entries.notes: No AI-origin detector will be adopted; it answers the wrong question.

entries.title: AP updates newsroom standards for artificial intelligence
entries.creator: Editor & Publisher, reporting on Associated Press standards
entries.attribution: Editor & Publisher, reporting on Associated Press newsroom AI standards. Paraphrased under attribution; no text reproduced.
entries.observations: Draws the human line around a function rather than a tool: reporting, sourcing, editorial judgment, and verification stay human, while summarization, transcription, translation, headline suggestion, and grammar cleanup may be assisted. Confirms verification and polish as structurally different activities. The staffing model behind it does not transfer to a single-author publication.

entries.title: app-demo-agent — timed voiceover workflow
entries.creator: Michael Boeding
entries.attribution: michaelboeding/skills app-demo-agent. MIT. Studied as a linked implementation reference; no Skill body copied.
entries.observations: The workflow establishes the visual timeline and duration before writing narration, measures rendered duration afterward, and prefers script adjustment over mechanical stretching. We absorb explicit predeclared timing contracts and script-first timing repair, not its app-demo-specific tolerances, voices, or mix settings.

entries.observations: Dedicated children's economics newspaper. Two articles read in full ('매매' word-origin piece, '디폴트' piece) plus one stagflation Q&A. Evidence of concrete/familiar-word-first sequencing before naming a 한자어 economic term, 한자 decomposition as an explanation device, and hedged (not flattened) uncertainty in a Q&A answer. See references/evaluations/econoi-childrens-economic-newspaper/. Recurring family-character device and column formats are house structure — do_not_copy, not adopt.

entries.title: ElevenLabs — pronunciation dictionaries and speech continuity controls
entries.creator: ElevenLabs
entries.observations: Official docs expose pronunciation dictionaries with model-dependent phoneme/alias support. The speech API also provides previous/next text and request IDs for long-form continuity plus best-effort seed repeatability; determinism is explicitly not guaranteed.
entries.notes: Related official API page: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/convert

entries.title: ElevenLabs — TTS models and text-to-speech guidance
entries.creator: ElevenLabs
entries.observations: Official model and TTS docs distinguish expressive Eleven v3, stable multilingual long-form lanes, and low-latency Flash v2.5. Control grammar is model-specific: v3 uses audio tags/punctuation and not SSML break tags, while supported non-v3 models accept break tags. Flash v2.5 documentation flags number/date/currency normalization as a latency-related risk.
entries.notes: Related official pages: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-creative/playground/text-to-speech and https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/product/core-capabilities/text-to-speech/how-can-i-add-pauses

entries.title: ElevenLabs Skills — text-to-speech Skill
entries.creator: ElevenLabs
entries.attribution: ElevenLabs text-to-speech Skill. MIT. Studied as a linked implementation reference; no Skill body copied.
entries.observations: The official Skill makes model choice, text normalization, request stitching with previous/next text, output mode, and usage tracking explicit. We absorb normalization/continuity/lineage patterns while keeping Eleven-specific voices, models, codecs, and SDK calls in the adapter layer.

entries.title: ElevenLabs — voice cloning overview and verification
entries.creator: ElevenLabs
entries.observations: ElevenLabs separates Instant and Professional Voice Cloning. Current PVC documentation requires verification and states that Professional Voice Cloning is for one's own voice; Instant Voice Cloning requires confirmation of right and consent. These controls are implementation safeguards, not editorial rights authority.
entries.notes: Related official PVC page: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-creative/voices/voice-cloning/professional-voice-cloning

entries.title: Gemini Developer API — pricing and media generation models
entries.creator: Google
entries.attribution: Google, Gemini API documentation. Capabilities and indicative prices paraphrased; no text reproduced.
entries.observations: A genuine programmable surface for image, speech, and video, unlike Gemini Notebook. Fit is by artifact kind: not for evidence visuals (a generative model cannot be trusted to render a number), plausible for infographic and audio, video deferred on cost with no editorial need. Pricing figures in the benchmark came from third-party summaries and are order-of-magnitude sequencing inputs, not a budget.

entries.title: Gemini Notebook API (formerly NotebookLM API) — what is available today
entries.creator: Notebook Clipper (third-party coverage)
entries.observations: Distinguishes the consumer product from the automation surface: no public consumer API for Gemini Notebook (ex-NotebookLM); REST endpoints exist under Gemini Notebook Enterprise via Gemini Enterprise. Establishes that an automated audio-brief pipeline would require an enterprise contract, not an API key. Read from secondary coverage; the authoritative source is Google Cloud documentation and was not verified directly in this pass.
entries.notes: Third-party NotebookLM-style podcast APIs exist and are not Google; routing article content through an unaffiliated intermediary is a provenance question before a technical one.

entries.creator: Google Cloud
entries.license: Google Cloud documentation terms; linked and paraphrased only

The '태풍이란?' entry and a related typhoon-formation passage define/explain using unglossed technical thresholds and physical-geography vocabulary with no concrete scene, analogy, or restatement — an audience-suitability anti-pattern (labelled child, register not actually adapted), distinct from baby-talk. entries.title: Reliability without Validity — LLM-as-a-Judge across agreement, consistency, and bias
entries.creator: arXiv preprint authors
entries.observations: Position, verbosity, and self-preference bias make a single holistic judge score unsafe as a release gate. Method adopted: decompose the rubric into discrete checks, rotate positions, validate against a human baseline, and keep deterministic checks out of the judge entirely. Quantitative magnitudes were read from secondary summaries and are not republished as findings.
entries.notes: Related: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.23178 (bias mitigation strategies). Rights not established for either; link-only.

entries.title: Slidev vs Marp vs reveal.js — code-first presentations
entries.creator: PkgPulse (third-party comparison)
entries.observations: Marp exports PDF and PPTX natively and is reportedly reliable and widely used in Korean developer practice — relevant because Korean-font templates are a known pain point. Slidev is more capable but turns the deck into an app; reveal.js needs external tooling to export. Marp chosen for the SUE-454 deck PoC so the whole chain stays textual: article Markdown → deck source → rendered deck.

entries.title: Headless Mermaid rendering outside the Node/Chromium path
entries.creator: merman project
entries.observations: Mermaid source is text and now renders headlessly to SVG/PNG/PDF without Puppeteer or a browser, which makes diagram artifacts regenerable in CI. At least one project in this space claims byte-identical geometry across architectures; that claim is unverified here and is a reason to shortlist, not a guarantee to design around. SUE-453 should test it and record the result.
entries.notes: Vendor claim, not replicated.

entries.title: NoizAI Skills — TTS Skill
entries.creator: NoizAI
entries.observations: The TTS Skill separates simple narration from timeline-accurate mode and stores voice/speed/emotion or reference-audio settings per segment. We absorb free-versus-timed narration and per-segment delivery-state patterns, not backend-specific cloning/emotion controls or fixed CPS heuristics.

entries.title: OpenAI API — custom voices and consent
entries.creator: OpenAI
entries.observations: Current custom-voice documentation limits the feature to eligible customers and requires separate consent and sample recordings whose voice identity must match. Confirms that provider-level consent is part of adapter governance while editorial policy remains independent and may be stricter.

entries.title: OpenAI Skills — curated speech generation Skill
entries.creator: OpenAI
entries.attribution: OpenAI curated speech Skill. Apache-2.0. Studied as a linked implementation reference; no Skill body copied.
entries.observations: The Skill separates exact input text from short labeled delivery instructions, distinguishes single/batch execution, validates important rendered clips, records final text/instructions/flags, and recommends one targeted iteration. We absorb those process boundaries without its provider/model/voice defaults.

entries.title: OpenAI API — text to speech
entries.creator: OpenAI
entries.observations: Official Speech API documentation describes /v1/audio/speech, gpt-4o-mini-tts instruction-based control, streaming, multiple audio formats, multilingual input including Korean, and a required disclosure that TTS audio is AI-generated. The instruction parameter does not apply to legacy tts-1/tts-1-hd. Model snapshots support version pinning.
entries.notes: Related official model page: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-4o-mini-tts

entries.title: Social Media Skills — AI voiceover Skill
entries.creator: Social Media Skills / WoopSocial
entries.attribution: Social Media Skills AI voiceover Skill. MIT. Studied as a linked implementation reference; no Skill body copied.
entries.observations: The Skill treats script-for-the-ear plus delivery direction as the main quality driver, loads shared brand/voice context before audio choices, and keeps consent/disclosure as a boundary. We adapt this to Suengj voice + content register while rejecting universal short-sentence rules, social hooks, and provider-led defaults.

entries.title: Vega-Lite — a grammar of interactive graphics
entries.creator: Vega project, University of Washington Interactive Data Lab
entries.observations: Chart specifications are JSON, so the spec is a text artifact that can be diffed, reviewed, versioned, and hashed; SVG output gives direct font control, which matters for Korean typography and Pretendard parity with suengj-com. Chosen for evidence visuals because the spec — not the rendered image — is the artifact, making byte-level regeneration possible.
entries.notes: License not verified in this pass. Nothing is copied, so it does not gate; verify before vendoring any spec or theme.
